_note: Prompts are the LOOK we want, not the narration. A narration is written for a viewer; a prompt is written for a model. In depth-conditioned mode the structure comes from the control pass, so these describe materials, period and light - which is what the model actually has freedom over. REVISED 2026-09-18: the first pass produced extremely low-key output on a01 and a03 because the prompts asked for 'deep shadow'. VACE follows lighting language literally, so these now state the exposure explicitly.
a01: Photorealistic 1825 Victorian tunnelling works, interior, brightly and evenly lit. A massive riveted cast-iron tunnelling shield fills the frame: twelve vertical frames across three levels, thirty-six open cells, dark pitted iron plate with visible bolts. Strong warm lamp light across the whole face of the shield so every frame and rivet is clearly visible; the shield is the brightest object in frame. Wet clay walls above and below, a curved brick tunnel bore behind, airborne dust. Documentary cinematography, shallow depth of field, well-exposed, clearly readable. Period-accurate 1825. No modern objects, no text.
a02: Photorealistic close view inside a single cell of a Victorian tunnelling shield. A thick rough-sawn timber board is drawn back to reveal dark wet blue-grey clay. Iron screw jacks above and below are braced against fresh brickwork. Warm lamplight from the left, hard shadows, muddy clay, coarse timber grain, riveted cast-iron plate. Documentary detail, shallow depth of field. Period-accurate 1825. No modern objects, no text.
a03: Photorealistic view straight down a Victorian tunnel under construction, evenly and clearly lit. A cast-iron tunnelling shield advances into the clay face; newly laid brick lining curves away behind it, with timber props and a short section of rail. Bright warm work-lamps along the tunnel so the iron grid, the brickwork and the clay are all plainly visible. Deep perspective, well-exposed, no crushed blacks. Period-accurate 1825. No modern objects, no text.
